text:
Maya (Sales): Incoming from BlueOak — they attached a 70-question security questionnaire and flagged two contractual clauses: data-retention export controls + BYOK requirement. POC needs to run on our hosted infra. deadline = Fri COB. can we triage?
Jon (AE): thx maya. who owns the questionnaire response? and is BYOK negotiable for POC?
Maya (Sales): cc @Sam (Security Eng) — sales asked me to route. BYOK is a hard ask from their legal, but they said maybe a temporary exception for POC if we can prove isolation + ephemeral keys.
Sam (Security Eng): OK. need to see the exact clause text. upload the questionnaire link pls and highlight the BYOK + export bits. also we need to know: 1) is customer data involved in POC? 2) retention timeframe they expect?
Maya (Sales): link: https://blueoak.example.com/qna/BOQ-2026-001 (public link they shared). they said POC will use synthetic data but want contract language that covers data egress controls. retention asked = "30 days" in doc.
Lee (SE): for POC hosted we can provision a dedicated sandbox on dedicated capacity (short-lived). isolation + token rotation during run covers most concerns. technical checklist I propose:```- provision dedicated GPU pool
- enable KV prefix caching disabled
- ephemeral API keys rotated daily
- restrict egress via security groups```
Sam (Security Eng): looks good. for BYOK: standard practice is BYOK for production only. for POC we can offer customer-supplied keys in a managed wrapper if legal signs off. will need evidence for: SOC2 controls for key management, KMS integration doc, and network isolation proof.
Nora (CS): I can draft the POC-specific appendix for legal that limits BYOK scope to: "POC-only, ephemeral keys, no production data, max 30 days" — will need sign-off from legal. ETA 48h if I get the highlighted clauses.
Jon (AE): pricing note: BlueOak asked about POC discounts — they want committed price per tested route. Maya, can you confirm estimated token volume? if low we can offer a free credit + discounted Dedicated day-rate.
Maya (Sales): estimated ~250k tokens total for a 2-week POC. they asked about burst capacity for demo day.
Lee (SE): for demo-day surge we can add burst-capacity config. I'll add a config snippet they can review:```{ "dedicated": { "gpupool": "small-multi", "burst": true, "max_qps": 200 } }```
Sam (Security Eng): next steps for security intake: 1) Sam to annotate the CAIQ/SIG mappings for flagged items (BYOK, export, retention) 2) Nora to draft POC appendix 3) Legal review (cc: legal@redwood) 4) Provide SOC2 + KMS evidence pack 5) decide BYOK-for-POC exception
Maya (Sales): deadline reminder — they want our responses by Friday COB. can we hit that?
Sam (Security Eng): compressed timeline but feasible if legal reviews fast. I'll start annotating now.
security-bot: Intake recorded: ticket #SR-2026-842 created, owner set to Sam (Security Eng), priority: high, due: 2026-05-07 17:00 UTC.
Nora (CS): I'll start the appendix draft and ping legal. pinging @legal-team — please advise on BYOK POC language. :eyes:
Jon (AE): thanks team. Maya — I'll prepare the POC pricing note to attach to the appendix (free credit + 50% day-rate for dedicated days).
Maya (Sales): copying the timeline here: - today: annotate + draft appendix - +24h: legal review - +48h: finalize responses and send to BlueOak. tagging @Sam for evidence list.
Sam (Security Eng): uploading checklist to the ticket and will attach KMS/SOC2 links.
Lee (SE): I'll prep the sandbox provisioning playbook for the day we greenlight. small note: for export-control clause we need to confirm which regions their reviewers consider 'export'. ask BlueOak clarification.
Maya (Sales): good call. I'll ask them to clarify region restrictions now.
Nora (CS): moving to action items in the ticket. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
